scope: Focused primary-source architecture review; not an exhaustive systematic review. Sources read at abstract/README/documentation level unless explicitly noted. No external implementation was copied.

references.title: Hill Climb Racing — Gymnasium RL Environment
references.license: GPL-3.0 (repository declaration); original assets and upstream provenance not cleared
references.key_idea: An HCR-like Box2D/Gymnasium environment with PPO baselines and comparisons of action and reward designs.
references.relevance: An existing baseline design and a warning that reward improvements can favor slow wheel motion rather than useful progress.
references.reuse: Literature comparison only; no source, sprites, datasets, or checkpoints reused.
references.limitations: The discrete three-action and scalar motor-speed spaces omit independently held simultaneous pedals. Reported simulator scores do not establish transfer or one-hour real-game competence.

references.title: Hill-Climb-Racing-AI
references.license: No repository license identified in the inspected landing page; reuse permission unverified
references.key_idea: Neuroevolution applied to a browser hill-climbing game recreation.
references.relevance: Motivates an evolutionary comparison and a separately rendered simulation.
references.reuse: Conceptual review only; no code or media reused.
references.limitations: A clone is not the installed commercial game. No reviewed evidence establishes calibrated dynamics, independent pedals, or governed transfer.

references.title: AI-Hill-Climb-Racing
references.license: GPL-3.0 (repository declaration)
references.key_idea: NEAT evolves controllers in a Matter.js browser clone.
references.relevance: Provides another example of derivative-free policy search on cheap simulation.
references.reuse: No implementation or assets reused.
references.limitations: Its physics and observations are not validated against the installed game; GPL code is not included in the MIT implementation.

references.title: Hill Climb Racing AI — Vision-Based Driving Agent
references.license: No repository license identified in inspected landing page; external dataset rights not audited
references.key_idea: Behavioral cloning predicts driving inputs from labeled 64×64 gameplay frames.
references.relevance: Shows a screen-observation pathway and motivates a small visual imitation baseline using our own recorded actions.
references.reuse: No source, dataset, model, or footage reused.
references.limitations: Three labels exclude simultaneous pedals. HUD masking removes useful fuel information. Random frame splitting could leak temporally adjacent samples; independent episode splits are required here.

references.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
references.license: Paper cited only; no third-party code license relied upon
references.key_idea: A clipped policy objective permits multiple minibatch optimization epochs per on-policy rollout.
references.relevance: A relatively compact, measurable initial policy learner.
references.reuse: Published equations inform an original implementation; no implementation copied.
references.limitations: PPO clipping does not guarantee improvement. Collection cost, optimization cost, and reward design remain workload dependent.

references.title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
references.license: Paper cited only; no code reused
references.key_idea: Exponentially weighted temporal-difference residuals trade advantage-estimate variance against bias.
references.relevance: Defines the advantage estimator for the PPO baseline.
references.reuse: Published algorithmic idea only.
references.limitations: Discount and trace parameters alter the effective horizon. True terminal states and time-limit truncations require different bootstrap handling.

references.title: Stable-Baselines3: Reliable Reinforcement Learning Implementations
references.license: MIT (library)
references.key_idea: Consistent, tested PyTorch RL implementations with established environment interfaces.
references.relevance: External algorithm reference and potential baseline; official PPO documentation supports MultiBinary and recommends testing frame stacking before recurrence.
references.reuse: No copied source; install as an optional comparator only if included in the actual dependency manifest.
references.limitations: Default vector wrappers and small-network GPU use may not maximize this host's throughput. Runtime measurements decide.

references.title: Recurrent PPO — Stable Baselines3 Contrib
references.license: MIT (library)
references.key_idea: PPO with LSTM state carried through sequences and reset by episode-start masks.
references.relevance: A reproducible recurrent comparator for partially observed vehicle dynamics.
references.reuse: Documentation informs interface tests; no implementation copied.
references.limitations: Sequence batching, hidden-state reset, and evaluation state handling add complexity. Recurrence must beat stacked observations at equal elapsed training time.

references.title: Gymnasium vector environments
references.license: MIT
references.key_idea: Standard single/vector environment contracts separate policy learning from simulation.
references.relevance: A stable interface for seeded reset, observations, actions, terminal flags, and batching.
references.reuse: Package dependency and API contract; no vendored source.
references.limitations: Autoreset conventions differ across libraries. Preserve final observations and test masks explicitly before training.

references.title: Box2D and pybox2d
references.license: Current Box2D: MIT; inspected pybox2d: Zlib
references.key_idea: Rigid bodies, contact handling, and joints provide a general basis for vehicle simulation.
references.relevance: Candidate replacement if measured errors implicate suspension or collision dynamics in a simplified original model.
references.reuse: Not adopted by this review; no source copied.
references.limitations: Current Box2D and historical Python bindings are distinct versions with different APIs/licenses. Neither supplies calibrated HCR behavior automatically.

references.title: PufferLib: Making Reinforcement Learning Libraries and Environments Play Nice
references.license: MIT (library)
references.key_idea: Environment compatibility wrappers and efficient vectorization reduce training-system overhead.
references.relevance: Candidate throughput framework once profiling establishes a collection bottleneck.
references.reuse: Review only; no framework implementation copied.
references.limitations: The 2024 paper and the current 4.0 repository are different revisions. Published throughput is not a measured Windows/HCR result; native build feasibility is unverified.

references.title: Sample Factory: Egocentric 3D Control from Pixels at 100000 FPS with Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
references.license: Paper cited only; code license not audited because no code selected
references.key_idea: Decouple collection and learning while controlling off-policy lag to use one machine efficiently.
references.relevance: Explains why larger process counts alone may fail and why learner utilization and policy lag should be recorded.
references.reuse: Systems ideas only.
references.limitations: Asynchrony changes algorithm behavior and adds correctness costs. Its headline frame rate cannot be transferred to this simulator.

references.title: Asymmetric Actor Critic for Image-Based Robot Learning
references.license: Paper cited only; no code reused
references.key_idea: Train the critic with simulator state while restricting the actor to deployable image observations.
references.relevance: Privileged values may improve learning without making the deployed policy depend on unavailable state.
references.reuse: Architecture idea for a planned ablation only.
references.limitations: An actor receiving true simulator velocity, contact flags, or hidden vehicle parameters is still privileged unless a validated pixel/history estimator supplies them.

references.title: Policy Distillation
references.license: Paper cited only; no code reused
references.key_idea: Transfer a trained policy into a smaller student or consolidate multiple teachers.
references.relevance: Potentially reduce real-game inference time and provide vision training targets from a privileged simulator teacher.
references.reuse: Planned experimental idea only.
references.limitations: Student learning, teacher generation, and any demonstration collection consume time/prior data and must be accounted for. Teacher-state coverage may not cover student mistakes.

references.title: Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World
references.license: Paper cited only; no assets/code reused
references.key_idea: Vary rendered scenes so a visual model does not depend on one simulated appearance.
references.relevance: Motivates bounded appearance/noise randomization for synthetic perception labels.
references.reuse: Idea only.
references.limitations: Object-localization transfer does not establish vehicle-control transfer. HCR artwork is not licensed by this paper.

references.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Robotic Control with Dynamics Randomization
references.license: Paper cited only; no code reused
references.key_idea: Vary simulated physical parameters during training to improve robustness to model mismatch.
references.relevance: Compare a fixed calibrated model with physically bounded parameter distributions.
references.reuse: Published idea; any implementation is original.
references.limitations: Randomization is not calibration. Unbounded or implausible parameter ranges may slow learning or encourage conservative behavior.

references.title: Preparing for the Unknown: Learning a Universal Policy with Online System Identification
references.license: Paper cited only; no code reused
references.key_idea: Condition a broadly trained policy on dynamics parameters inferred from recent state/action history.
references.relevance: An interpretable starting point for adapting to vehicle changes.
references.reuse: Planned architecture idea only.
references.limitations: Different physical parameters can produce similar short visual trajectories. Identification uncertainty and held-out vehicle testing matter.

references.title: RMA: Rapid Motor Adaptation for Legged Robots
references.license: Paper cited only; code license not audited because no code reused
references.key_idea: A base policy uses an environment representation estimated online by a separate adaptation module.
references.relevance: Compare latent history context against explicit vehicle IDs and full recurrent policies.
references.reuse: Planned research idea only.
references.limitations: Robot results do not imply HCR performance. Rapid test-time adaptation relies on prior simulator training whose full cost must remain visible.

references.title: RL²: Fast Reinforcement Learning via Slow Reinforcement Learning
references.license: Paper cited only; no code reused
references.key_idea: A recurrent policy learns an adaptation procedure through task-distributed training and retained within-task memory.
references.relevance: Conceptual comparison for adaptation from observations, actions, rewards, and terminations.
references.reuse: Review only.
references.limitations: Do not call an ordinary recurrent PPO model meta-RL. Task distributions, cross-episode memory rules, and slow pretraining must be specified.

references.title: World Models
references.license: Paper cited only; no model/code reused
references.key_idea: Learn compact visual and temporal latent representations, then train a compact controller using them.
references.relevance: Alternative if raw visual dynamics become the dominant data-efficiency bottleneck.
references.reuse: Review only.
references.limitations: Latent reconstruction fidelity need not preserve task-critical failures; model training and data collection costs count against the budget.

references.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models (DreamerV3)
references.license: MIT (official implementation); no reuse in initial stack
references.key_idea: Learn a world model and optimize an actor-critic with imagined trajectories across varied domains.
references.relevance: A model-based candidate when real experience is expensive enough to justify greater learner compute.
references.reuse: Review only; no JAX implementation copied or installed by this review.
references.limitations: No evidence here establishes a one-hour HCR advantage. Compare total elapsed time including model learning, warm-up, evaluation, and prior data; the repository also cites a later Nature publication.

references.title: Curriculum Learning
references.license: Paper cited only; no code/content reproduced
references.key_idea: Order training examples by difficulty to influence optimization and generalization.
references.relevance: Compare easy-to-hard terrain scheduling against training directly on the fixed target distribution.
references.reuse: Idea only.
references.limitations: Curriculum quality must be evaluated on unchanged held-out targets. An easier training distribution can create apparent improvement without competence gains.

references.title: Evolving Neural Networks through Augmenting Topologies
references.license: Paper cited only; implementation license not used
references.key_idea: Evolve network structure and weights using historical markings, speciation, and gradual complexity growth.
references.relevance: Motivates a derivative-free competitor to gradient learning.
references.reuse: Review only.
references.limitations: A fixed-topology evolution-strategy or cross-entropy baseline must not be labeled NEAT. Population evaluation may consume substantial experience.

references.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
references.license: Paper cited only; no rliable code reused
references.key_idea: Account for uncertainty and robust aggregate performance when evaluating stochastic RL.
references.relevance: Use multiple training seeds, intervals, and matched evaluation conditions before claiming algorithm superiority.
references.reuse: Methodological guidance only.
references.limitations: Many episodes from one trained policy do not replace independent training seeds. Small seed counts warrant exploratory language.
